Elements of Art: Elements of art
The basic visual building blocks artists work with
Line
A mark with length and direction
Contour line
A line describing the edge of a form
Implied line
A visual path suggested rather than drawn
Shape
A flat enclosed area defined by an edge
Geometric shape
A regular mathematical shape such as a square or circle
Organic shape
An irregular shape suggesting living forms
Form
A three-dimensional volume or its illusion
Space
The area within and around a composition
Positive and negative space
The object versus the emptiness around it
Texture
The tactile surface quality, real or implied
Value
The relative lightness or darkness of a tone
Color
The visual sensation produced by different wavelengths of light
Composition
The overall arrangement of elements in a work
Principles of Design: The ways artists arrange the elements of art
The distribution of visual weight in a composition
Balance achieved with unequal but visually weighted elements
Elements radiating from a central point
Strong differences that create visual interest
The dominance given to a focal area
Where the viewer's eye is drawn first
The path the eye travels through a work
Reusing an element to build unity
Size measured against a familiar reference
The sense that a work holds together as a whole
Differences that keep a work from becoming monotonous
Elements that relate comfortably to each other
Drawing Fundamentals: Gesture drawing
A rapid sketch capturing movement and overall energy
Contour drawing
Drawing the outline and interior edges of a form
Blind contour drawing
Drawing an edge without looking at the paper
Line weight
Varying thickness to suggest depth and emphasis
Sighting
Using a pencil at arm's length to measure proportions
Proportion in figure drawing
The adult figure standing roughly seven and a half heads tall
Basic shapes method
Constructing complex objects from simple geometric forms
Negative space drawing
Drawing the gaps to improve accuracy of the subject
Foreshortening
Compressing a form receding toward the viewer
Still life
A drawing of arranged inanimate objects
Sketchbook practice
Regular informal drawing that builds skill and ideas
Drawing media
Graphite, charcoal, conte, ink, and coloured pencil
Hardness of pencils
H grades being harder and lighter, B grades softer and darker
Fixative
A spray protecting charcoal and pastel from smudging
Value and Shading: A graduated strip from white to black used as a reference
The brightest area where light strikes directly
The middle value between highlight and shadow
The darkest band on the form turning away from light
The shadow an object throws onto a surface
Light bouncing back into a shadow from a nearby surface
The gradual darkening on a curved surface
Parallel lines used to build value
Overlapping sets of parallel lines to deepen value
Smoothing tones for a continuous gradient
Strong contrast of light and dark to model form
The direction light comes from, which governs all shading
Keeping every shadow logical to a single light source
Perspective: Linear perspective
A system creating depth using converging lines
Horizon line
The line representing the viewer's eye level
Vanishing point
The point where parallel lines appear to converge
One-point perspective
A system with a single vanishing point, used for head-on views
Two-point perspective
A system with two vanishing points, used for corner views
Three-point perspective
A system adding a third point for dramatic height or depth
Orthogonal lines
The receding lines converging at a vanishing point
Eye level
The height from which a scene is viewed, setting the horizon
Atmospheric perspective
Distant objects appearing lighter, bluer, and less detailed
Overlapping
Placing one object in front of another to signal depth
Diminishing size
Objects appearing smaller as they recede
Foreground, middle ground, background
The three depth zones of a composition
Picture plane
The imaginary flat surface the image is projected onto
Distortion in perspective
Objects near the frame edge stretching unnaturally
Color Theory and Mixing: The circular arrangement showing colour relationships
A colour made from two primaries
A colour mixed from a primary and an adjacent secondary
The pure identity of a colour
How vivid or dull a colour appears
Adding its complement to reduce intensity
Opposites on the wheel producing strong contrast
Neighbours on the wheel producing harmony
Reds and yellows that advance versus blues that recede
An object's actual colour under neutral light
A pleasing relationship among selected colours
Working from few colours to unify a piece
The dull result of overmixing complements
Painting Techniques: Acrylic paint
A fast-drying water-based paint that becomes waterproof
Watercolor
A transparent water-based medium built from light to dark
Oil paint
A slow-drying medium allowing extended blending
Gouache
An opaque water-based paint with a matte finish
Underpainting
A preliminary monochrome layer establishing value
Wash
A thin diluted layer of paint
Wet-on-wet
Applying paint into a still-wet layer for soft blending
Dry brush
Using little paint on a dry brush for broken texture
Glazing
Applying a transparent layer over dry paint to shift colour
Impasto
Thick paint applied so brushstrokes stand up from the surface
Scumbling
Dragging opaque paint loosely over a dry layer
Fat over lean
The oil painting rule of increasing oil content in each layer
Gesso
The primer preparing a surface to accept paint
Support
The surface painted on, such as canvas or panel
Palette
The surface used for mixing, and also the colours chosen
Brush types
Round, flat, filbert, and fan, each producing different marks
Printmaking: Printmaking
Creating multiple original images from a prepared matrix
Matrix
The block, plate, or screen carrying the image
Edition
The set of prints pulled from one matrix
Artist's proof
A print outside the numbered edition kept by the artist
Relief printing
Printing from the raised surface of a carved block
Linocut
A relief print carved from linoleum
Woodcut
A relief print carved from a wood block
Brayer
The roller used to apply ink to a relief block
Registration
Aligning multiple colours or pulls accurately
Intaglio
Printing from lines incised below a plate's surface
Etching
An intaglio process using acid to bite lines into metal
Drypoint
An intaglio process scratching directly into the plate
Lithography
Planographic printing based on the repulsion of oil and water
Screen printing
Forcing ink through a stencilled mesh screen
Monoprint
A print with variable elements, producing a unique result
Reversal in printing
The printed image appearing mirrored from the carved block

Shaping a pliable material such as clay
Pouring material into a mould to reproduce a form
An internal support structure holding a sculpture's shape
A form projecting from a background surface
A work viewable from every side
The oven that fires clay into ceramic
Unfired dried clay, at its most fragile
The first firing hardening clay before glazing
A glassy coating fused to ceramic in a second firing
Kneading clay to remove air pockets that would cause explosions
Roughening and wetting clay edges so joints hold
The perceived bulk of a form versus the space it encloses
Sculpture designed for one particular location
Mixed Media: Artwork combining more than one material or technique
Composing by adhering paper and flat materials to a surface
Combining photographic fragments into a new image
An everyday item repurposed as art material
An unaltered manufactured object presented as art
Building meaning and depth through stacked materials
Choosing a glue appropriate to the materials joined
Acid-free supplies that resist yellowing and decay
Treating a support so mixed materials adhere reliably
Using fabric, sand, or paper to create real surface variation
Work transforming an entire space rather than hanging on a wall
Work where the idea takes precedence over the object

Work showing range across media and approaches
